title: ESMFold’s pair representation carried more readable geometric information
summary: A readout study found that ESMFold’s intermediate representations added up to 0.32 AUROC for recovering relationships within folded structures over the upstream ESM-2 representation. Single-position attributes were already largely recoverable upstream. The result distinguishes two kinds of information in the model.

source_review.scope: §§3–4, readout and circuit-attribution checks; PDF front matter

evidence.tested: Learned dictionary readouts were compared with features from the upstream sequence model. The authors also checked whether changing interpretation prompts shifted the apparent division between representation types.
evidence.unknown: The finding concerns information recoverable from one trained folding model. It does not establish that the attributed directions are causal or describe how a protein folds in a cell.
evidence.ai_role: Fitted sparse dictionaries exposed features from the trained folding network. Comparative readouts assessed where geometry-related information became more accessible.
